Macassar Abandoned

By: Catherine Rice | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The community of Macassar, a small town near Cape Town, is under siege. The once peaceful community has been taken over by criminals, with residents feeling abandoned in every way by authorities.

Unique Selling Point:
Macassar, a small town near Somerset West and the Strand, is home to over 50,000 people. It was once a tranquil community, home to many fishermen and workers at the neighbouring dynamite factory. It was also well known as a pilgrimage site, for the founder of the Islamic faith in the Cape, Sheikh Yusuf, who died in 1699. His kramat, his grave and sacred shrine, still stands today and is regularly visited by devout Muslims. Much more recently, in 1991, the Macassar Beach Pavilion was built, attracting families from across the Cape Flats. However, in 2004, due to financial problems it was closed, and nature reclaimed the once colourful slides, swimming pools and buildings, burying them under mountains of sand. Nothing remains of the water park, its succumbed to the South Easter driven sands and vandals have long since made off with what remained of value. Its now just a faded memory for Macassar residents who feel, just like the water park that attracted so many, they too have been forgotten and abandoned by authorities, and have become an easy target of criminal gangs.

Summary:
Macassar is a small town on the outskirts of Cape Town, situated on the False Bay coastline, near Somerset West and the Strand. It's home to over 50,000 people. In the past decade, conditions in the town have deteriorated dramatically, and the once peaceful community has become the target of outside criminals. Elderly residents who have lived there their whole lives recall much happier times, before it became a dumping ground for the bodies of murder victims, its canals crime-infested. It's no longer a safe place, gangs from inside and outside the area are active, with little being done by the police to stop them. In the space of a week earlier this year the bodies of four murder victims were dumped in the area. And extended load shedding and power outages have contributed to the daily struggle to survive, particularly in the hours of darkness, of those who live there.

Script:


VO 1 Macassar beach - for decades, a popular fishing spot on the False Bay coastline.

VO 2 Once, a safe and peaceful place.

VO 3 But, for years now, the fabric of Macassar in the Western Cape has been slowly but steadily unravelling..

VO 4 Saturday, May the 27th marked the start of a week that Felicity Solomons will never forget.

VO 5 The body of a woman, who had been raped and murdered, callously dumped on Macassar beach.

UPSOUND Felicity Solomons / Community leader July 21 Clip 5139 Time code 00:15 “The people that first catch it was the fishermans, they were first on scene, its a dumping site now”.

VO 6 Felicity was born and raised in Macassar.

VO 7 In recent years, she says its become the target of criminals from outside the area..

UPSOUND Felicity Solomons / Community leader July 21 Clip 5098 Time code 01:14 Since I grow up things have changed tremendously and you have to be afraid for the kids 01:35 On their way to school on their own things happen like kidnapping and stuff like that.

VO 8 Felicity tries to keep the children in her area safe and escorts them to and from school.

VO 9 It’s a far cry from the memories of her youth when she spent long afternoons at Macassar beach pavilion.

UPSOUND Felicity Solomons / Community leader July 21 Clip 5098 10:08 Yoh that was lekker days, if you want to know lekker days that was lekker days, you got to the beach with your two piece, the pavilion was so beautiful. 11:03 Now, its a sad sad story that is where it all ends.. 11:39 There’s nothing left, nothing left at all.

PRESENTER LINK: (clip 5129 July21) It’s hard to imagine now, but this was once a bustling seaside resort popular with locals, all that’s remains today are these last pieces of rubble of the Macassar Beach Pavilion which was built in 1991.

VO 10 In 2004, the City of Cape Town abandoned the water park due to vandalism and maintenance costs. It was soon buried by shifting sands. Some blame its location near the sea. In 2020, the remaining structure was demolished in just seven days, leaving little trace.

VO 11 For Etienne Williams, Macassar beach is part of his family’s heritage - he comes from a long line of fishermen.

UPSOUND Etienne Williams / Macassar Resident July 20 Clip 4808 Time code 00:38 People moved to Macassar because of the village known for fishing. We had all the fishing, everything here, but its changed from being a fishing village to being a place of murders and drugs and prostitution.

VO 12 The community blames the increase in crime on the lack of police resources and unplanned power outages.

VO 13 It’s become a dangerous place. Just a few weeks ago, a fifteen year old boy was stabbed and Etienne was called to help.

UPSOUND Etienne Williams / Macassar resident 20 July clip 4805 Time code 01:30 You know how sad it is when a fifteen year old boy just dies in your arms because there wasn’t someone with experience to help him. He basically bled to death.

VO 14 Etienne’s own son is about the same age as the stabbing victim..

UPSOUND Etienne Williams / Macassar Resident Clip 4806 / Time code: 01:21 My son has this dream, he wants me to drop him by the beach in school holidays to fish alone, I had the same dream, but in my time it was fine, I could walk from my house to the beach and nothing would happen. Today, he can’t walk to the shop without fearing for his life.

VO 15 The community feels abandoned by authorities.

VO 16 Despite its rich history dating back several centuries, the area is rapidly becoming a soft target for criminals from other areas.

PRESENTER LINK: July 21 Clip 5166 The Sheikh Yusuf kramat here in Macassar in the Western Cape is an old Islamic pilgrimage site. This was once a safe and peaceful community for raising a family and those seeking a sense of belonging, but with the recent and gristly discovery of four dumped bodies in the space of a week, all that has changed.

VO 17 Ebrahim Rhoda is a former teacher who has spent many years researching the history of Islam at the Cape..

UPSOUND July 20… Ebrahim Rhoda / Reseacher Clip 4918 Time code 01:08 You are sitting within the cradle where Islam was established at the Southern tip of Africa by this great luminary who was buried here in 1699.

VO 18 Sheikh Yusuf was an Islamic scholar and leader, exiled from Indonesia because of his threat to the commercial interests of the Dutch.

Ebrahim Rhoda / Researcher clip 4918 Time code That is why this place here Macassar very historical named after the town where Sheikh Yusuf was born.

VO 19 But, the town of Macassar is no longer only associated with historical significance..

VO 20 Instead, it has become known as a dumping ground for dead bodies.

UPSOUND Peter Helfrich / Ward Coucillor 20 July Clip 5015 Time code 00:13 On the 28th of May a second body was found here where we are standing. (photos courtesy of Mark Baatjies)

VO 21 Peter Helfrich is the local ward councillor.

VO 22 He’s been having to survive on only four hours of sleep a night due to his efforts to protect his community..

UPSOUND Peter Helfrich / Ward councillor Clip 5002 Time code: 02:21 People were also very frustrated because just the day before a body was found on Macassar beach. Time code: 03:21 the person was stabbed by broken bottle in head and neck.

VO 23 Shockingly only days later yet another body was found on the 1st of June… also off the Macassar road, hidden amongst bushes..

VO 24 And then, almost unbelievably, a fourth body was discovered..

VO 25 Four bodies found in a week made headlines, but it still hasn’t brought the assistance the community desperately needs.

VO 26 The longer the hours of darkness, the higher the probability of criminal incidents…but just how reliable is the power supply to Macassar?

VO 27 Here, electricity is supplied by Eskom. Peter believes the ageing infrastructure is the reason for the frequent and extended power outages: a situation ripe for criminality.

UPSOUND Peter Helfrich / Ward Councillor Clip 4992 Time code 03:27 In our ward as soon as loadshedding is supposed to end it does not end. And this sometimes last for days. The criminals know this and they take advantage of this and this is when they come to our ward to commit crime.

VO 28 And with an under resourced police service, Macassar residents are easy prey.

UPSOUND Peter Helfrich Clip 4992 Time code 00:14 There is only one police van available most of the time in this ward.. On one shift, there is only two police officers available to serve us and we are more than 50,000 residents in this ward.

VO 29 Macassar residents turn to their community leaders as a last desperate resort.

UPSOUND Peter Helfrich Clip 5012 Time code 00:14 Unfortunately, people have lost faith in our police service and that is why they call me first.

EWN AUDIO (Felicity listening to radio) -

VO 30 As the shadows lengthen in Macassar, the call to prayer can be heard. (NATSOUND July 21 Clip 5196) (let this breathe)

VO 31 For those living here, the setting of the sun does not signify the peaceful end of a long day, but rather the beginning of rising anxiety for what could lie ahead.

VO 32 As dusk descends, anything is possible. Something these brave locals know too well.

UPSOUND Peter Helfrich / Ward Councillor July 21 Clip 5199 Time code 00:45 You all of us standing here is the last line of defence for the residents of the ward (addressing the group of neighbourhood watch members).

NATSOUND July 21/ Clip 5252 Time code 00:02 Just be very careful, this is a very hostile area

VO 33 Tonight, the metro police are accompanying members of the neighbourhood watch.

VO 34 Its loadshedding, and people disappear into the darkness.

PRESENTER LINK We contacted the police about the spike of crime in Macassar. In an email, the SAPS recognised the unprecedented crime wave and reported the allocation of further resources to addressing the problem.

VO 35 From being associated with the birthplace of Islam in South Africa, to becoming a dumping ground for the dead, Macassar residents remain afraid of the darkness that cloaks their community.

VO 36 Left on their own until authorities hopefully come to their rescue.

VO 37 Since that horrific week not long ago…only one arrest has been made in connection with the first body discovered on Macassar beach. A male suspect has been charged with the rape and murder of the female victim.

VO 38 Another one of the bodies has been identified as that of a homeless man. The circumstances surrounding his death remain unknown.

VO 39 But, for the other two, who they were and how they died, remains a mystery.
